title: Graph Mamba Operator: A Latent Simulator for Interacting Particle Systems
claim: A stacked encoder-decoder simulator whose core layer couples graph interactions and state updates in one input-dependent recurrence.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; compact stack beside detailed layer diagram with legend
description: The figure has two panels plus a legend. The left gray rounded panel, titled GraMO, shows a vertical stack. Node-position graphs with red velocity arrows enter at the bottom. They pass through an Encoder, then repeated GraMO Layer blocks (a brace marks 'Repeat x L'), then a Decoder, and come out as predicted graphs at the top. Red up-arrows link the stages. The large pink right panel, titled GraMO Layer, shows the detailed data flow. Node embeddings and edge indices go into a graph convolution. The output feeds several yellow trapezoid projection functions (f_dt, f_B, f_X, f_C, f_Z, f_X̃). Their outputs combine through dashed groups with multiply, add and einsum symbols into H_{t+1}, Y_{t+1}, LayerNorm, Output Projection and a residual sum. A color-coded legend on the far right marks learnable, input-dependent, fixed, token-mixer and state-variable elements.
caption: Overview. The model maps past graph sequences $\{\mathcal{G}_t\}_{t=0}^{T}$ to future trajectories $\{\mathcal{G}_t\}_{t=T+1}^{T+\Delta T}$ using $L$ stacked \method blocks. (Left) Overall pipeline. (Right) A single \method layer showing the discretized update and gated skip connection (see Appendix Algorithm [ref]).
abstract: Modeling interacting dynamical systems requires capturing spatial interactions alongside long-range temporal dependencies. Graph neural networks (GNNs) provide a natural representation but typically rely on autoregressive rollouts and treat spatial and temporal dynamics separately, leading to error accumulation over long horizons. Existing approaches also focus on local interactions and short temporal contexts, limiting their ability to capture multi-hop dependencies and global structure. We introduce the Graph Mamba Operator (GraMO), a latent-space simulator that integrates state-space models with graph-based interaction learning. In contrast to prior work that sequences nodes or applies spatial and temporal updates in separate stages, GraMO couples graph-based interactions and temporal state updates within a single recurrence. The update is linear in the latent state, with input-dependent coefficients that adapt across regimes. We evaluate GraMO on N-body systems, motion capture, and robotics datasets, achieving the lowest error across benchmarks and the largest gains in long-horizon prediction.
